title: Normal Distribution Explorer MicroSim
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Set the mean and standard deviation of a normal distribution and read the intervals that hold 68, 95, and 99.7 percent of the values.

educational.topic: The normal distribution and the 68-95-99.7 rule
learningObjectives: Students will be able to use the mean and standard deviation of a normal distribution to find the intervals that contain about 68%, 95%, and 99.7% of the values.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Parameter exploration on fixed axes with a pinned curve for comparison
keyQuestions: What happens to the curve when μ changes and σ stays the same?
Why does the peak get lower when σ gets larger?
Why are the three percentages in the table the same for every choice of μ and σ?
commonMisconceptions: A larger standard deviation makes the curve taller (it makes the curve wider and lower, because the total area stays 1).
The height of the curve at x is the probability of x (the height is a density, and probabilities are areas under the curve).
The 68-95-99.7 rule works for any data (it describes normal distributions, and skewed data can be very different).
Exactly 95% of values lie within 2 standard deviations (the area is 95.45%, and exactly 95% corresponds to 1.96 standard deviations).
assessmentOpportunities: Without the MicroSim, students state the interval that holds about 95% of the values of a normal distribution with a given mean and standard deviation (for example μ = 500 and σ = 100) and sketch how the curve changes if σ is halved.
